history.position: THIS COURSE TEACHES NO REPAIR HISTORY. The engine's review changes (extraction precision, recall and micro and macro F1 added beside accuracy, the near-tie golden) landed before its merge and before any lesson was written; they are provenance. The digest describes the engine as it is.

scopeSeams.logistic regression, log loss and classi: OWNED BY D2 mlcore. D5 imports logLoss from engines/dataai/ml.js, prints what it returns with its eps and clipping count, and takes the calibration set's probabilities as given inputs.
scopeSeams.data quality and near-duplicate identifi: OWNED BY D1 dataqc. D5 uses the exact duplicate EKD-058 for its tie only.
scopeSeams.the bootstrap as a general method, and P: OWNED BY the uncertainty course and D4 forecastml. D5's interval is a percentile of a statistic, labelled as a parameter percentile, never P10, P50 or P90.
scopeSeams.language models themselves: NOT BUILT. D5 evaluates the retrieval, answers and extractions a language-model copilot would produce, using fixture text; no model runs anywhere in the engine, the fixtures, the gates or the course, and no graded value depends on model output (digest section 4).

namingCollisions.relevant: a judged grade at or above the stated threshold, grade 1 by default; related is grade 1 itself. Sections 11, 24.
namingCollisions.hallucination: an unsupported claim, named with the engine's reason. Sections 10, 15, 24.
namingCollisions.grounded: supported by a cited and retrieved passage; never a statement about truth. Sections 15, 24.
namingCollisions.accuracy: correct cells over cells, named with its denominator. Sections 14, 24.
namingCollisions.score: a BM25 score or TF-IDF cosine, named with its method; never a probability. Sections 6, 7, 24.
namingCollisions.AI: the system being evaluated; the engine runs no model. Sections 1, 4, 24.

openItems.ENGINE FINDINGS: None blocking. The foundation found no engine defect and no unclear reason string; the three FINDINGS open questions are decided by the course as recorded under decisions.
openItems.DECISION relevantGrade: FINDINGS open question 1 (default grade 1 against 2). Kept at the engine default, grade 1 (trec_eval); the digest teaches the threshold as a stated setting and prints every mean at grade 1 and grade 2 (section 11), where the MAP order of the two systems reverses. The Professional capstone grades a MAP at grade 2 with the grade stated.
openItems.DECISION end of 2025: FINDINGS open question 2. Kept as a teaching example of how a deterministic check reads text (section 15); no engine change requested.
openItems.DECISION bin edges: FINDINGS open question 3. The course states the engine's edge rule and the library's (section 19, with the library table DERIVED in the dump and labelled so); the Expert capstone grades three Murphy terms at eight bins, where 2 dp probabilities sit on the interior edges 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75, so the library rule is a discriminated wrong method.
openItems.DECISION ECE not graded: On the Ekene calibration rows every bin is over-confident at 5, 10 and 15 bins, so ECE equals mean probability minus the base rate whatever the bins (digest section 18, asserted). The first capstone cut graded ECE at eight bins and the discriminate sweep found it blind to the bin count and the edge rule; it was replaced by the Murphy reliability term, which both move.
openItems.DECISION capstone values kept off coinci: Every graded value is checked against the vendored golden, the digest and every sibling wave's answer key (gate_capstone_leak directions 3, 6 and 7). The first cuts collided three times, each a simple fraction or a near-coincidence: the Associate capstone's supported fraction 4/7 printed in the digest as a system B F1, its MRR 17/24 in the golden, and the Expert capstone's reliability within ten tolerances of a golden number. The Associate capstone now runs five queries at cutoff 4 and five answers (one citing a passage that was not retrieved, so ignoring the retrieved lists is a discriminated wrong method), and the Expert capstone draws 122 calibration rows (a first choice of 124 put the within-bin covariance within ten tolerances of a fixture BM25 score at a shifting of 1000); the Professional bootstrap runs on seed 44 (seed 41 put the four-decimal rendering of its bound inside a digest figure). Every value clears the golden, digest, sibling and fixture sweeps.
openItems.DECISION Associate capstone cutoff 4: The Associate capstone states cutoff 4, where the teaching cutoff is 5: at 4 no capstone query has a tie at the cutoff and the mean recall and MRR clear the coincidence sweeps; the teaching digest keeps 5, the systems' own cutoff.
